newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ALBERT BELLE FILES FOR FREE AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALBERT BELLE FILES FOR FREE AGENCY.

text.p: Albert Belle, the Cleveland Indians' ill-tempered home run leader and a candidate for the American League Most Valuable Player Award, Monday filed for free agency.
Belle reportedly turned down a a five-year, $37 million offer from the Indians in March and then hit .311 with 48 homers and 148 RBI in 1996.
He is the first major star to delcare himself a free agent, but the Indians still very much hope to hold onto their big-hitting outfielder.
"All along Albert Belle and the Cleveland Indians organisation had the understanding that he would test the waters and file for free agency," Indians general manager John Hart said.
"We are looking forward to negotiating with Albert and his representatives in the very near future in the hopes of keeping him a member of the Cleveland Indians."
The free agent filing period began at the conclusion of the World Series and concludes at midnight November 14.
A total of 129 players are eligible to file, including Atlanta Braves ace pitcher John Smoltz, the leading cadidate for National League Cy Young honours.

Pitcher Jesse Orosco and third baseman Todd Zeile of the Baltimore Orioles, infielder Mark McLemore and pitcher Mike Stanton of the Texas Rangers and outfielder Mark Carreon of the Indians started the activity by filing for free agency Sunday.
